source.how: GET https://discord.com/login (no cookies, no auth) -> 575 /assets/*.js+css bundles listed in the HTML. The main bundle web.1cce76ccd5e996d2.js holds rspack module 696354, a require.context over the client sounds folder mapping "./<name>.mp3" to module ids; each of those modules is e.exports=n.p+"<hash>.mp3" with n.p="/assets/". The soundpack table is module 458640 (pack enum in 235079). To make sure nothing lives only in lazy chunks, the runtime chunk table (T.u, 5214 chunks) was used to download every lazy chunk; no other audio asset is referenced anywhere (only 4 .webm/.mp4/.mov UI videos).
source.js_saved_in: not kept (the Discord web client files used to find the sound list)

wav_format: 16-bit PCM, 44100 Hz, stereo (decoded with scripts/mf_decode.py, Media Foundation; 48 kHz files FFT-resampled to 44.1 kHz, mono duplicated to 2ch)

soundboard_note: Discord's default soundboard sounds. The client JS builds their URL as https://${CDN_HOST}/soundboard-sounds/${id} (module 102597 in web.1cce76ccd5e996d2.js, CDN_HOST = cdn.discordapp.com). Only the name list (GET /api/v9/soundboard-default-sounds) needs a login; the files themselves don't. HEAD requests on ids 0-300 (no cookies, no auth): ids 1-7 answer 200 audio/mpeg, everything else 404. Id 7 is byte-identical to id 6. Names were worked out from the audio (see name_evidence) against Discord's documented defaults: quack, airhorn, cricket, golf clap, sad horn, ba dum tss (the API docs example is sound_id 1 = quack). Saved as magneto/discord/soundboard_<name>.mp3.
